title: Cap. X Arg. V Minor: given/not-given distinction precedes human faith and perseverance — John vi. 37: coming to Christ depends on the Father's giving as antecedent cause
pass_a_gloss: Let us now come unto the Minor, and show that this discrimination of those given and not-given unto Christ precedes human faith and perseverance, precedes also absolute foresight of human unbelief and pertinacity. That it precedes faith and perseverance is gathered from those words, Whatsoever the Father gives me shall come unto me: and him who comes unto me I will not cast out, Joann. vi. 37. It is manifest from these words that to come unto Christ and to remain in Christ, which is to believe in Christ and to persevere in faith, depends from this giving of the Father, as from an antecedent cause.
pass_b_english: Now to the Minor: let us show that this distinction of those given and not-given to Christ precedes human faith and perseverance, and also precedes absolute foresight of human unbelief and pertinacity. That it precedes faith and perseverance is gathered from these words: Whatever the Father gives me will come to me; and him who comes to me I will not cast out (John vi. 37). From those words it is plain: coming to Christ and remaining in Christ — that is, believing in Christ and persevering in faith — depends on this giving of the Father as on an antecedent cause.
source_text: Veniamus nunc ad Minorem, et ostendamus hanc distinctionem datorum et non-datorum Christo antecedere fidem et perseverantiam humanam, antecedere etiam praevisionem absolutam infidelitatis et pertinaciae humanae. Quod fidem et perseverantiam antecedat ex illis verbis colligitur, Quicquid mihi dat Pater, ad me veniet: et eum qui venit ad me non ejiciam foras, Joann. vi. 37. Manifestum est ex hisce verbis, venire ad Christum et permanere in Christo, quod est credere in Christum et in fide perseverare, ex hac datione Patris, tanquam ex antecedente causa dependere.
